Use the `--workers` command line option. When deploying applications you will probably want to have some replication of processes to take advantage of multiple cores and to be able to handle more requests.[2] You can start multiple workers with the `--workers` command line option[3].

**With the `fastapi` command:**

```console
$ fastapi run --workers 4 main.py
```

**With `uvicorn` directly:**

```console
$ uv run uvicorn main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 --workers 4
```

The only new option here is `--workers` telling Uvicorn to start 4 worker processes.[4] In the output, it shows the PID of each process, `27365` for the parent process (this is the process manager) and one for each worker process[4].

The docs I found don't say how to choose the number of workers relative to your CPU cores.

**If you use containers:**
- On Kubernetes or another cluster, you would not want to have multiple workers in the container, for example with the `--workers` command line option. You would want to have just a single Uvicorn process per container (but probably multiple containers).[5]
- In special cases, such as a simple app on a single server or Docker Compose, you can set workers in your Dockerfile:

```dockerfile
CMD ["fastapi", "run", "app/main.py", "--port", "80", "--workers", "4"]
```

More details: https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/deployment/server-workers/ and https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/deployment/docker/
